title: Hybrid burst policy heuristics and safeties
author: Asha R. Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the heuristics, safety gates, and operational runbook for Redwood's hybrid burst scaling policy. The hybrid burst policy is responsible for temporarily increasing capacity beyond committed/dedicated pools by leveraging a combination of: (a) warm standby hosts in Dedicated, (b) burstable hosted capacity, and (c) opportunistic heterogeneous GPU attachments. The goal is to keep user-facing latency SLOs while controlling incremental cost and isolation risk.

Audience
- Platform engineers (owners of autoscaler, queueing, and routing)
- SRE and oncall for inference clusters
- Product owners who consume reserved and burst capacity

Key objectives
- Ensure 99th percentile request latency remains within configured SLOs for critical routes (default 99th <= 450ms for chat/generation on latency tier).
- Limit incremental burst spend to a configurable burn-rate per tenant and per org pool (default 2x baseline for no more than 30 minutes per incident).
- Avoid noisy-neighbor impact to Dedicated customers: isolation and migration must trigger before interference thresholds.

Policy model and decision surface
1) Inputs captured every 15s:
   - Queue depth per back-end model-server shard
   - Per-tenant token/sec and request/sec rates
   - GPU utilization (smoothed 1m, 5m) and memory pressure
   - Tail latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) per route
   - Prefix/KV cache hit-rate and cache-serving latency
   - Cost burn estimator (estimated $/token over the next hour)

2) Heuristics (ordered):
   a) Prefer warm standby pool expansion: if warm_count > 0 and p99_latency_exceeds(SLO, 10%), activate up to min(warm_count, scale_needed).
   b) If warm exhausted, evaluate hosted-burst eligibility: allow hosted-burst only if tenant_burst_credits_available AND org_burn_rate < org_threshold.
   c) Opportunistic heterogeneous attachments (e.g., A10 -> A100 mix): only for non-isolated workloads and when interference_score < 0.2.
   d) Model-variant fallback routing: if high-latency persists > 90s, transparently route new requests to lower-latency model variant (quantized or shorter-context).

Safety gates (hard abort conditions)
- Interference gate: if cross-tenant GPU memory contention > 12% above baseline, abort new heterogeneous attachments and initiate migration of noisy tenants within 30s.
- Cost gate: if projected incremental burst spend > configured monthly-burst-cap for org, immediately throttle burst requests and notify billing-runbook.
- SLA gate: if SLO degradation across >3 regions simultaneously, disable cross-region burst and fail open to canary fallback model.

Metrics and dashboards
- Required metrics (emit at 15s or 1m aggregation):
  - burst_capacity_allocated (gpus, vCPUs)
  - burst_cost_estimate_hourly_usd
  - bursted_tenants_count
  - interference_score (0-1) per pool
  - p99_latency_by_route (baseline vs current)
  - cache_hit_rate_by_prefix

- Dashboards to create:
  1) "Burst Capacity Overview": time-series of allocated burst gpus, cost estimate, and tenant list with active bursts.
  2) "Interference & Safety": interference_score heatmap, migration actions, and abort events.
  3) "Per-Org Burn & Thresholds": per-org burn rate, remaining burst-credits, and projected spend.

Alerting thresholds (first responders: platform-oncall)
- P0: interference_score > 0.6 on any dedicated pool for 3 consecutive minutes -> page SRE_primary.
- P1: burst_cost_estimate_hourly_usd > 3x baseline AND projected_1h_spend_increase > $2500 -> Slack alert @platform-costs and ticket to finance.
- P1: >5 tenants in burst state with p99_latency still > SLO after 2 minutes -> page platform-oncall.

Operational runbook (incident steps)
1) Detection & triage
   - On page: check dashboard "Burst Capacity Overview" and "Interference & Safety".
   - Confirm if latency is due to queue build-up or backend service degradation (run quick query: SELECT queue_depth, p99_latency FROM metrics where route=$route over last 5m).
2) Immediate mitigation (first 5 minutes)
   - If interference_score high, execute: kubectl patch priority-eviction for noisy-tenant -> target=evict; start migration job: /usr/local/bin/migrate-tenant --tenant $id --target-pool=isolated.
   - If cost-gate hit, disable hosted-burst via: /opt/platform/ctl burst disable --org $org_id; notify billing.
   - If cache miss surge, warm-up strategy: enable prefix prefetch for top-10 prefixes for affected routes.
3) Recovery & follow-up
   - When p99_latency returns within 10% of baseline for 10 minutes, roll back migration throttles and reconcile billing ledger.
   - Create post-incident ticket with timeline, root cause, and action items. Include exact timestamps of bursts and migrations.

Rollout and experimentation plan
- Canary stage (2 weeks): enable hybrid-burst for 3 low-impact tenants in staging region, monitor interference and cost for 72h/windows.
- Beta stage (6 weeks): expand to 20% of tenants with opt-in flag; expose burst-visibility UI in Console for those tenants.
- GA (Q3 2025): default policy for non-enterprise tenants with documented thresholds and per-org caps.

Policy configuration example (YAML snippet)
- Note: example fields are editable via platform-config service.
- policy: hybrid_burst_v1
  targets: ["non-isolated", "burst-enabled"]
  warm_pool_preference: true
  warm_pool_limit: 0.6
  per_org_max_burn_multiplier: 2.0
  per_burst_max_duration_minutes: 30
  interference_abort_threshold: 0.12
  heterogeneous_attachment_allowed: true
  heterogeneous_max_utilization: 0.85
  metrics_poll_interval_seconds: 15

Retrospective practices and success criteria
- Every post-incident review must include: load trace, autoscaler decisions timeline, costs incurred, and test replays.
- Success criteria for GA: average incremental cost per tenant for burst events < $120, fewer than 1% of burst events trigger interference aborts, and 99th latency SLO maintained in 95% of burst incidents.

Ownership and related pages
- Owners: platform-scaling (primary), infra-observability (dashboards), billing-integration (cost gating).
- Related pages (internal links):
  - /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/priority-tenant-slicing-and-burst-credit-economics-2026
  - /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/predictive-scale-and-eviction-playbook-2026
  - /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/runtime-cost-instrumentation-and-alerting-2026

Open items (roadmap)
1) Integrate model-quality-aware burst: do not burst for routes with active quality regression flags. Target Q2 2025.
2) Implement fine-grained per-model quantized-variant routing to reduce need for burst. Target Q4 2025.
3) Add automated tenant compensation workflow for cost/availability impacts. Target Q1 2026.

Appendix: CLI examples and queries
- Disable hosted burst for org:
  sudo platformctl burst set --org=acme-corp --enabled=false
- Query current burst tenants:
  curl -s "https://platform-metrics/api/v1/bursts?state=active" | jq '.tenants[] | {id,org,allocated_gpus,started_at}'
- Evict noisy tenant quickly:
  /opt/platform/ops/evict-tenant --tenant-id $TENANT --reason "gpu_interference" --dry-run=false
